onboarding.cloud.haveServerDescription: Connect it with one command. About 2 minutes.
onboarding.cloud.needServerDescription: Get one from Hostinger, Hetzner, Contabo, DigitalOcean or any other provider. About 5 minutes.
onboarding.cloud.pathSubtitle: Dokploy runs your apps on a server you own. Pick what fits you.
onboarding.cloud.exploreHint: You can explore the dashboard. Nothing can be deployed until a server is connected.
onboarding.cloud.exploreHintTrial: You can explore the dashboard. Nothing can be deployed until a server is connected, and your trial won't start until then.
onboarding.cloud.payNowSkipTrial: Pay now and skip the trial
onboarding.cloud.planSubtitle: Subscribe now and skip the trial. You can change plans at any time.
onboarding.cloud.pickProviderSubtitle: Any VPS works. These four work well with Dokploy, or use your own. Create a server, then come back here to connect it.
onboarding.cloud.providerStep1: Create a server with Ubuntu and at least 2 GB of RAM.
onboarding.cloud.providerStep2: Open the server's web console, or SSH in as root.
onboarding.cloud.providerStep3: Come back here to get the command that connects it.
onboarding.cloud.anotherProviderDescript: Vultr, Linode, OVHcloud, AWS Lightsail, a home server or any VPS with root access.
onboarding.cloud.progressSaved: Your progress is saved. We'll email you a link back to this step within the hour.
onboarding.cloud.fail.ssh.title: Dokploy couldn't open an SSH connection to the server
onboarding.cloud.fail.ssh.body: The command reached Dokploy, but Dokploy couldn't sign in back as root on port 22. A firewall is blocking that port, or SSH doesn't allow root to sign in with a key.
onboarding.cloud.fail.ssh.fix1: In your provider's firewall or security group, allow inbound TCP on ports 22, 80 and 443.
onboarding.cloud.fail.ssh.fix2: Make sure SSH listens on port 22 and allows root to sign in with a key.
onboarding.cloud.fail.ssh.fix3: Run the command from the Connect screen again on the server.
onboarding.cloud.fail.os.title: This server isn't running Ubuntu or Debian
onboarding.cloud.fail.os.body: Dokploy found a different operating system, so it stopped before changing anything.
onboarding.cloud.fail.os.fix1: Open your provider's dashboard and rebuild the server with Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12.
onboarding.cloud.fail.os.fix2: Run the command from the Connect screen again on the rebuilt server.
onboarding.cloud.fail.memory.title: This server has less than 2 GB of RAM
onboarding.cloud.fail.memory.body: Dokploy needs 2 GB of RAM and 30 GB of disk to build and run apps, so it stopped before installing anything.
onboarding.cloud.fail.memory.fix1: Resize the server to at least 2 GB of RAM in your provider's dashboard.
onboarding.cloud.fail.memory.fix2: Wait for the resize to finish.
onboarding.cloud.fail.memory.fix3: Run the command from the Connect screen again on the server.
onboarding.cloud.fail.disk.title: This server has less than 30 GB of disk
onboarding.cloud.fail.disk.body: Dokploy needs 2 GB of RAM and 30 GB of disk to build and run apps, so it stopped before installing anything.
onboarding.cloud.fail.disk.fix1: Resize the server's disk to at least 30 GB in your provider's dashboard.
onboarding.cloud.fail.disk.fix2: Wait for the resize to finish.
onboarding.cloud.fail.disk.fix3: Run the command from the Connect screen again on the server.
onboarding.cloud.fail.limit.title: Your plan doesn't include another server
onboarding.cloud.fail.limit.body: The server is reachable, but your current plan has no free server slots, so it wasn't added.
onboarding.cloud.fail.limit.fix1: Open Settings → Billing and add a server to your plan.
onboarding.cloud.fail.limit.fix2: Run the command from the Connect screen again on the server.
onboarding.cloud.fail.setup.title: Installing Docker and Traefik didn't finish
onboarding.cloud.fail.setup.body: Dokploy connected to the server, but the install stopped before it was ready.
onboarding.cloud.fail.setup.fix1: Make sure the server can reach the internet and nothing else is using ports 80 and 443.
onboarding.cloud.fail.setup.fix2: Check again from this page. Dokploy retries the install.
onboarding.cloud.connectSubtitle: One command: paste it on your server and Dokploy finds it by itself. Dokploy checks the server first and installs Docker for you.
onboarding.cloud.runAsRoot: Run this on your server as root
onboarding.cloud.commandExplanation: It adds Dokploy's public SSH key and tells Dokploy where the server is. Dokploy then installs Docker for you and shows the progress here. It works once and expires in 1 hour.
onboarding.cloud.pageUpdatesItself: This page updates by itself when the command runs.
onboarding.cloud.pageUpdatesByEmail: This page updates by itself when the command runs again. We've emailed you these steps too.
onboarding.cloud.own.git.title: From a Git repository
onboarding.cloud.own.git.desc: GitHub, GitLab or any Git URL.
onboarding.cloud.own.image.title: From a Docker image
onboarding.cloud.firstDeployWorked: Your first deploy worked, on your own server. Open it, or deploy your own app next.
onboarding.cloud.trialRunsUntil: Your trial runs until {{date}}. Two days before it ends, we'll ask you to choose a plan and add a card.
onboarding.cloud.serverReadyTrial: Your server is ready. Your 7-day trial starts now and runs until {{date}}, with no card needed yet.
onboarding.cloud.serverReady: Your server is ready. Deploy something to it right away.
onboarding.cloud.oneClickTemplate: One click, with no repository or build settings. See an app running on your server before you connect your own code.
onboarding.cloud.deployFailedTryAnother: The deployment failed. Try another template, or open the project to read the logs.
onboarding.cloud.deployingToServer: Deploying {{name}} to your server. This usually takes a minute or two.
